findings.note: HB 825, Election Improvements, filed with Echevarria and Scott as primary sponsors (bill page lists Echevarria first). Among other things it changes the ID items for absentee ballot requests: the request form would ask for the last four digits of the Social Security number plus one of a driver license number, a special ID card number, or the voter's date of birth. It also lets a voter who cannot attach an ID photocopy to a returned absentee ballot use an alternative affidavit that cites that as a reasonable impediment. It also bans ranked choice voting, shortens early voting, and adjusts rules for election-related activity near polling places. Last action: referred to House Rules on 2025-04-09; no further action shown.
subjects: ID number with mail or absentee ballot request

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (member vote record shows Aye, 66 to 47)
findings.note: Voted aye on second reading of HB 958, Election Law Changes. The ratified text requires voter registration applications to affirmatively state US citizenship before processing (with a 30-day notice and sworn statement route if the question is left blank), requires the State Board to create a process to remove voters flagged as non-citizens in a federal database, and speeds removal of deceased voters. The text reviewed is the ratified edition (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf); the text voted on at second reading may differ.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register (citizenship statement on registration form)

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, motion to concur in Senate changes (member vote record shows Aye, 62 to 47)
findings.note: Voted aye on the motion to concur on HB 958, Election Law Changes, the final House vote before ratification. Ratified text includes a citizenship statement requirement on voter registration applications and a process to remove voters flagged as non-citizens from a federal database.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register (citizenship statement on registration form)

findings.motion: House Bill 825, Election Improvements, primary sponsor (filed 2025-04-08, referred to Rules 2025-04-09)
findings.note: Echevarria is a primary sponsor of House Bill 825, Election Improvements. The bill text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H825v0.pdf) would bar ranked choice voting, shorten early voting, and change the forms of identification for an absentee ballot request: the request form would ask for the last four digits of the Social Security number plus a driver licence number, special ID card number or date of birth, and a voter who cannot attach a photocopy of ID to a returned absentee ballot could use a reasonable-impediment affidavit with the same identifiers. The bill was referred to the Rules committee and the page shows no later action.
subjects: ID number to request an absentee ballot

findings.motion: Election Law Changes, Second Reading (House roll call 758)
findings.note: Brian Echevarria voted Aye on second reading of House Bill 958, Election Law Changes (66 Ayes, 47 Noes). The ratified text requires a voter registration application to affirmatively state citizenship, sets a 30-day notice process with a statement under penalty of perjury when the answer is blank, and sets a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens from a federal database. The Governor vetoed it on 2026-08-17.
